1.why: All MFA routes call auth()/verified(), which derive the account solely from the server-side session's accountId (never a client-supplied ID), so MFA settings are bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Verification codes are stored per account (a.identityCode, session-bound backup code digests) and checked only against the session owner's record, so one user's code cannot verify another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only clears failedMfa counters; the session ID is not rotated and no other sessions for the account are invalidated, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encrypt()/Enc type) and backup codes are stored as SHA-256 digests with a pepper, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, codes, and session IDs come from bytes(), which uses crypto.getRandomValues (CSPRNG), including the 6-digit codes via six().

6.why: The session cookie is __Host-prefixed with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token and codes only in in-memory variables—no localStorage/sessionStorage or readable cookies are used.

7.why: Server-side validators (email, phone, code, recovery regexes), type checks, and a 4KB body limit validate all user input before use.

8.why: The client renders all dynamic values via textContent/createElement (status, codes, secret), innerHTML is used only with static templates, and a nonce-based CSP blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The server issues no redirects and client navigation is hash-based, restricted to a fixed allow-list of internal views, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: sec() sets CSP (with per-request nonces and frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and no-store caching.

11.why: cookie() emits the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, and the __Host- prefix.

12.why: Although server errors are generic with no stack traces and secrets stay out of URLs, the client deliberately writes the provisioning secret, mock OTP, identity code, and recovery codes to the on-page Logs panel and console via log(), so these secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code is marked used/cleared after success and expires in 5 minutes, the pending TOTP secret is single-use with a 10-minute expiry plus 30-second time window, and backup codes are flagged used on redemption.

14.why: Failed MFA, identity, and login attempts increment counters that trigger 15-minute lockouts after 5 failures (MAX/LOCK), enforced at both session and account level.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID (rotation), sessions enforce 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
